newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Tajiks see '97 cotton harvest soaring to 600,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Tajiks see '97 cotton harvest soaring to 600,000 T.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Tajikistan planned to harvest about 600,000 tonnes of raw cotton this year, said a Tajik agricultural official, quoted on Friday by Russia's Interfax news agency.
Radzhab Kadirov, a senior official at Tajikistan's Agriculture Ministry, said the Central Asian state would begin sowing next week, with 247,500 hectares to be sown.
But Kadirov said that only 49 percent of land was fully ready for spring sowing and that there was a shortage of seeds.
The agency said the republic produced 312,400 tonnes of raw cotton last year, down from 417,000 tonnes in 1995, and that Tajikistan exported only 95,000 tonnes of raw cotton in 1996.

The country's cotton crop has declined dramatically during the country's bloody four-year civil war. In Soviet times, the cotton harvest used to total around 900,000 tonnes. --Almaty Newsroom +7 3272 509410
